correctness.rationale: Every word has a unique first/last-a gap decomposition. Pattern a b^r a exists iff the total internal-b count k is at least r; scattered ab count is A times trailing-b plus the index-weighted internal gaps. Summing weak compositions of k yields z^k Gaussian(A+k-2,k) and summing all trailing counts yields the displayed exact finite polynomial. Reversal complements ab counts to AB-C. At A=2, eliminating the trailing count gives an exact parity cutoff; comparing three consecutive coefficients proves strict valleys for all odd r>=3 and nondecreasing-to-midpoint counts for even r. A separately staged executable check directly enumerated 264 parameter cases/104105 word examinations and confirms the algebraic formula; the proof, not finite data, handles infinitely many parameters.

value.rationale: The newly studied 2026 question seeks probabilities of a scattered pattern in languages specified only by Parikh entries. This theorem converts those unknown conditional probabilities for the infinite, naturally symmetric family ab^r a into explicit all-parameter coefficient extraction; the sharp two-a parity switch shows that imposing longer scattered avoidance breaks the Gaussian/known-r=2 unimodality even though positivity and reciprocity survive. It is a structural rather than merely numerical finite observation and isolates a natural shape boundary. The classical r=2 case is not promoted as a discovery.
